about: The ledger contract: every event kind in ledger.jsonl, the script that writes it (or the list of scripts that do), and its fields.

Each field's type is string, number, array (a list), object or id (a Discord id: a string of digits, which --check also takes as a whole number, the form team-log wrote before), or a list of the strings it may be.
Every line has ts (UTC, like 2026-10-22T01:00:00Z), task (T<n>) and event; note (a string) is allowed on every kind, and other fields are allowed.
Lines from strict_from on must meet their kind's fields; earlier lines are legacy and only need ts, task and event.
Legacy lines keep shapes no kind has now: closes by hand with no lists, and plan-ready, which is not a kind, since a planner's report is done and a plan put to Daniel is asked.
Read by ledger_append in bin/lib/team.sh (through bin/lib/ledger.jq) and printed by team-log --help.

opened.about: story is the backlog story the task builds (team-open --story), which team-merge marks done

interview-thread.about: team-thread --interview: the task's thread under the interview channel, where a planner interviews Daniel

launch.about: request is the link to Daniel's Discord message, on an ops launch; model is the --model the session launched on, from the project's models in the registry, absent on the default

closed.about: a legacy task's lists are empty; the hand-written legacy closes before strict_from have none

merged.about: approval: the word it merged on, head (a merge-approved of the PR at its head) or plan (a standing merge-preapproved of its project); by names Daniel's Discord message either way

asked.about: a decision put to Daniel; discord_message: the question's first message in the task's thread, which team-inbox links

answered.about: Daniel's answer to the asked of its id; discord_message: the message it was read from, never logged twice for one ask

paused.about: since: when the park began, when it is logged after the fact

blocked.about: a worker stopped by an obstacle; the next launch or resumed clears it; since: when the park began, when it is logged after the fact

held.about: since: when the park began, when it is logged after the fact

waiting.about: a task parked on Daniel or something outside the team; the next launch or resumed clears it; since: when the park began, when it is logged after the fact

resumed.about: clears held, blocked, paused and waiting

review.about: sent_back: the numbers of the findings sent back to the builder before the merge, each a blocking finding, a correctness, security or real-data note, or a plain note on a line the PR adds or changes, never one before lists; findings: the count of each kind, exactly blocking, correctness, security, real-data, note-change (plain notes on lines the PR adds or changes) and note-before (plain notes on code it did not change), each a whole number; before: the numbers of the plain notes on code the PR did not change, each queued as a follow-up; guarded: the guarded areas the reviewer found the change touching, each one of ci, dependencies, migrations, settings, permissions and secrets, empty for none

gate-run.about: one per gate run, at its end: run is the gate's run id, head the commit it ran on, cause why it repeats an earlier run on the same PR, minutes each step's minutes as no-mistakes axi status --run prints them

merge-approved.about: Daniel's word on the PR at url, one of the task's pr events, at head, the full sha the ask named, which a pr event of url, or a review of the task since url's first pr event, logged, its discord_message sent no earlier than the first of those that logged it; team-log requires head of every new line, and earlier lines without it hold for any head; legacy lines name only the number

merge-preapproved.about: Daniel's plan-time word on the task's PR in project, its discord_message an answer to the task's latest asked of id ask, sent no earlier than it, which it settles; scope the repository paths the plan may change, each a file or a directory ending in /; it stands until a later merge-preapproval-withdrawn of project, and the latest of a project is the one read

merge-preapproval-withdrawn.about: Daniel withdrew the standing merge-preapproved of project, in discord_message

branch-renamed.about: the task's branch in project is branch from now on, as when the gate rewrote the remote branch and the builder carried its commits to a new one; the latest opened, worktree-added or branch-renamed of the project names the task's branch there

retro-schedule.about: Daniel's word on how often a retro runs, read by team-retro from the latest across the ledger; every_hours 0 stops the retros

stowed.about: one per open task at a handoff, or per task team-stow stows: worktrees as {project, branch, head}, with uncommitted: true for one whose changes the checkpoint kept as wip/<project>/T<n> on the team home's origin; roles the task's unfinished work, each role launched since its last stowed that nothing ended (ledger.jq's unfinished_roles), which the other machine or the resume relaunches; sessions the roles whose sessions the stow stopped, for the record (before 2026-10-25, roles held those); cause level for a stow to free the machine for the team's resource level, handoff (or absent, as in every line before team-stow) for a handoff

worktree-moved.about: team-open --resume, when this machine's worktree for the task in project is not the recorded one

injection.about: outside text that asked role to act: source is where it was (a URL, a path, a command, or <collection>/<_id>), text what it asked, never the personal details it held

rehome-failed.about: a worktree of the task in project that team-open --resume could not make on machine, reason the first line team-open printed; it stands until a later opened, worktree-added, worktree-moved, rehomed or worktree-returned of the task in project

rehomed.about: team-open --resume, when it makes the worktree at its recorded path while a rehome-failed of the task in project stands; made anywhere else, the worktree-moved clears it
